claim: The byte a 3D type prints `Speaker/Phones` against does not switch an output on or off and does not change a level. It picks between two renderings of the same placement, and which rendering is in use changes how the two channels are separated as a function of frequency. On the median plane the two renderings are the same thing: at the front and directly behind, where the placement leaves the two channels level, every one of a hundred and thirteen twelfth octaves agrees to within two tenths of a decibel and so does the total. Everywhere else they differ, and the difference turns over with frequency -- the speaker rendering separates the channels more below a hundred and twenty five hertz and less above two kilohertz, at 24 of the 24 placements that can show it -- every one of them -- and by up to 13.8 decibels in a band. The speaker rendering is also about a decibel and a half louder over the two channels together. The whole of it is antisymmetric about the front: the placement on one side returns the negative of its mirror to within 2.6 dB at the worst of 15 pairs, which is what says this is a property of the byte and the placement rather than of the takes. The same four are returned by the other type that places by a byte, read after the placement it names has arrived, so this is what the stage does and not what one type does.
why_not_named: What the two modes are for is not what was measured. The measurement is of two channels leaving two sockets; a mode intended for loudspeakers is about what arrives at two ears after those channels have crossed in the air, and nothing here reaches that. The name says which byte, not which acoustics.

measurements.why: The placement byte swept with this byte at Speaker, thirty-one settings, one per placement the azimuth class measured the byte to reach. The held block is what says the two records differ in this byte and in nothing else.

The same sweep with this byte at Phones, at all hundred and twenty-eight settings. The thirty-one the other record holds are a subset of these, so the contrast is taken at settings both were asked at rather than at settings one was interpolated to.

The same takes read a band at a time, which is where the turn-over with frequency is. A broadband balance cannot carry it: the two renderings move opposite ways at the two ends of the band set and what is left over the whole of it is whichever end the stimulus has more energy in.
The other side of the same comparison, on the same band set.

01 70 in Phones, the settings that sweep's own takes said it had not reached. The same five settings the other type is cited at -- the two poles, the front, and the two the byte moves furthest -- so the two types are read at the same placements rather than each at whichever suited it.
The same takes read per band, on the same 113 twelfth octaves the other type was read on. What the turn-over with frequency and the mirroring are read off.

document_rows.why: Every row the page prints this pair of names against. All four are 3D types and all four put the byte at the same address, which is what makes the question one question; only the fourth was measured.

era_priors.claim: A part of this period offering a binaural placement two output modes offers the plain one for headphones and, for loudspeakers, one that compensates for each speaker also reaching the far ear. That compensation is a filtered, inverted copy of each channel added to the other, and because the crosstalk it fights is nearly complete at low frequencies and small at high ones, it needs a large correction low and a small one high.
era_priors.why: It says why the difference between the two renderings would turn over with frequency in the direction it does rather than in the other, which is the shape that was found. It carries none of the claim: every figure above was measured, and the prior is not evidence that the mechanism is the one named.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The difference had been flat with frequency, or larger high than low. Both were possible outcomes of the reading and neither happened.

adds: Four printed parameters had no claim within reach of them by any reading of the coverage, and this is the first measurement of any of them. It also puts a second byte on the placement class's records without a take being made: the azimuth sweep was run twice and the second run has been sitting beside the first as a control rather than as evidence about its own byte.

the_contrast.what: Speaker less Phones at the thirty-one settings both records hold, in the balance between the two channels and in the two of them together. The floor is the coarser of the two records' own repeats at that setting, which is between a hundredth and five hundredths of a decibel.
the_contrast.and_what_they_are: The front and the two ends of the byte. The azimuth class measured the two ends to be one place -- directly behind -- and measured the level there to be the level at the front, so all three are the median plane. Two renderings of a placement with nothing to separate are the same rendering, and the byte is measured to do nothing at exactly those three.
the_contrast.why_the_level_difference_is_not_the_two_: The two records are two invocations, so a decibel and a half of level between them is exactly what a trim moved between takes would look like. It is not one: a trim shifts every setting together and these three sit at two hundredths of a decibel while their neighbours sit at a decibel and a half. The level difference appears and disappears with the placement inside one pair of records, which nothing outside the unit does.

the_turn_over_with_frequency.what: Speaker less Phones in the separation between the channels, a band at a time, collected into five ranges by the median of the bands in each that clear the pair's own floor. A positive number is the speaker rendering separating the channels further in the direction the placement already puts them.
the_turn_over_with_frequency.read_as: Below 125 Hz the speaker rendering separates further, by a median 7.7 dB over the placements that show it; above 2 kHz it separates less, by a median 7.4 dB. The two ends carry opposite signs at 24 of the 24 placements away from the median plane and away from the four below.
the_turn_over_with_frequency.and_it_mirrors: Every placement's five numbers are the negative of its mirror's about the front, to within 2.60 dB at the worst of 15 pairs. The two halves of the sweep were taken minutes apart and neither record knows about the other, so a difference that mirrors is the byte and not the session.

four_placements_that_answer_differently.what: At these four the two channels together do not move at all -- two hundredths of a decibel, the same as on the median plane -- while the balance moves more than at any of their neighbours, and the band shape is one sign across the whole range instead of turning over.
four_placements_that_answer_differently.why_it_is_not_a_bad_take: They mirror. The pair two placements either side of the front returns the negative of the other to within 2.6 dB in every range, and so does the pair two either side of the back, on records taken separately -- and the repeats inside each setting agree to 0.04 dB. Two spoiled takes would have to have been spoiled in mirror image.
four_placements_that_answer_differently.what_this_does_not_say: What is different about them. They are not adjacent to each other and they are not the neighbours of the median plane -- the placements either side of the front do move the total, and these sit one further out. Nothing here explains that and nothing here is offered as an explanation.

alternatives.reading: The speaker rendering is the headphone one with a filtered copy of each channel subtracted from the other -- a crosstalk canceller, which is what the two names are for.

separated_by.why_not_separable: Not by this archive, and not for want of a run. What a canceller is defined by is what reaches two ears past two loudspeakers, and every figure here is what leaves two sockets. The two channels' magnitudes alone cannot separate a subtraction across from any other pair of filters that produces the same two magnitudes, because the phase between the channels is what makes a cancellation a cancellation and the balance reading discards it. This repository does hold a stage that reads the phase between two channels, and pointing it here is a run -- but it would still return a pair of transfer functions rather than a cancellation, so it is named here as what would sharpen the reading and not as what would close it.

alternatives.reading: The other three 3D types answer this byte the same way, so this is a fact about the 3D stage rather than about this type.

separated_by.observable: The balance between the two channels at every placement its byte reaches, with this byte at each of its two values, on the second of the two 3D types that place by a byte.

predicts.one stage: The four things read on the first type, again: the two renderings identical where the placement is on the median plane, a difference elsewhere that turns over with frequency in the same direction, an antisymmetry about the front, and the speaker rendering louder in the total off the median plane.
predicts.four stages: Anything else, including no difference at all.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: The contrast measured on the first type reaches 13.8 dB in a band and 7.45 dB in the balance, and the balance stage repeats a setting to between a hundredth and five hundredths of a decibel.

run.settings: one inside each of the thirty-one positions, in both output modes
held: the type's own speed, direction and turn all at nought, as before
a wait between writing the block and striking the note, which the run above did not have and which is what it is missing

measure_the_wait_first.why: A wait is a parameter and not a constant. This archive has already read a type where the figure taken after ten seconds was most of the way wrong and arrival belonged to the entry rather than to the byte, so a length assumed here would be the same mistake with a different type's name on it.
measure_the_wait_first.how: One setting furthest from the block that arrived, taken at two waits far apart, with the two takes of each. The wait is long enough when the two takes of the same setting agree to what the first type repeats to, and when the longer wait returns what the shorter one did.

run.why: The same observable, asked after the placement has arrived. What it buys is unchanged: the whole of the first type's reading repeated on a second type -- the identity on the median plane, the turn-over with frequency, the antisymmetry about the front and the level difference off the median plane.

the_two_types_this_cannot_be_asked_on.why: Neither takes a placement as an argument. `01 44` is printed with a pre delay, a chorus rate and a chorus depth, and `01 57` with three delay times and three delay levels; where the image sits is what those make and there is no byte to move it with. So the observable this alternative is separated by does not exist on them, and the alternative stays open over those two however the run comes back. What could be asked of them is whether the byte changes anything at all, which is a weaker question and is not this one.

asked_once_and_did_not_answer.what_was_run: The placement byte at one setting inside each of the thirty one positions, in both output modes, on `01 70` with its speed, its direction and its turn all written to nought, two takes a setting, the block written and read back once per setting.
asked_once_and_did_not_answer.why_it_does_not_answer: At most settings the two takes of one setting did not agree, and they disagreed the same way at setting after setting rather than scattering: about +2.9 against +12.2 decibels in Phones and about +3 against +5.6 in Speaker. A byte the unit ignored leaves both takes in one place, so two takes landing in two places is the placement moving between them rather than the byte failing to arrive.
asked_once_and_did_not_answer.what_it_does_establish: Over a contiguous block in the middle of the range the two takes agree to hundredths of a decibel and match the first type's reading of the same byte to about two hundredths -- twelve settings of it in Phones, +13.15 against +13.17 at byte 35, +0.14 against +0.14 at 63, -10.51 against -10.52 at 79. Where the placement has arrived, the two types read one table.
asked_once_and_did_not_answer.the_first_type_does_not_do_it: `01 71` repeats every one of its hundred and twenty eight settings to within a few hundredths, in the same sessions and on the same stimulus, which is what puts this on the type that turns rather than on the stage, the stimulus or the rig.
not_established: Why the block that has arrived sits where it does in the range.
Whether the placements furthest from it arrive at all, or only travel.
Whether writing the turn to nought is doing anything.

alternatives.taken_up_by: The run was made, could not answer, and was made again. The second type that places by a byte returns every one of the four: identical on the median plane to 0.01 dB against the first type's 0.01, the turn-over with frequency at 24 of the 28 placements that can show it against the first type's 24 of 28 and in the same direction, antisymmetric about the front to 0.08 dB against 0.06, and the speaker rendering louder over the two channels together at 25 of 28 by a median 1.57 dB against 26 of 28 by 1.56. Per band the five range figures mirror to 1.52 dB at the worst of 15 pairs, against 2.60 on the first type and at the same placement and the same range. Not `ruled_out_by`: this is the reading that turned out to be right, and the claim above is revised to say it. What the first attempt at this run returned was the movement -- that type reaches its placement over seconds -- and what it cost is written in the record beside it rather than dropped.

refuted_by: The two renderings coming back identical at a placement off the median plane, or differing at the front. Or the difference having one sign across the whole band set at every placement, which would make it a filter on the output rather than something that depends on how far apart the two channels already are. Or the two halves of the sweep failing to mirror, which would put the difference in the session rather than in the byte.
what_it_would_change: A renderer reading a file that sets this byte has to switch rendering and not just a level, and the two renderings are not a fixed filter apart -- what the byte does depends on where the placement is. A renderer that treated the byte as cosmetic would be wrong by up to 13.8 dB of channel separation at the ends of the band set, and by a decibel and a half of level everywhere off the median plane.
what_this_does_not_settle: Which filters the two renderings are. What is measured is the difference between two magnitudes at a hundred and thirteen bands and thirty-one placements, and a pair of transfer functions is not recoverable from that without the phase between the channels. Nor the four placements above. Nor anything about the other three types, which is the standing alternative with a run against it.

the_second_type_that_places_by_a_byte.what: The second type that places by a byte returns all four of the things the first type's reading says, read after the placement has arrived. Both types go through one piece of arithmetic and the first type's figures do not move: its records hold two takes a setting, where the median this uses and the mean it used before are one number.
the_second_type_that_places_by_a_byte.why_the_first_run_could_not_say_this: It was made without a wait. Read off those takes the second type returns 3.38 dB apart on the median plane where the first returns 0.01, four of its twenty-eight placements can show the turn-over instead of all twenty-eight, and the antisymmetry that is 0.06 dB on the first type is 18.99. None of that is the byte: the same takes read after arrival give 0.01, twenty-eight and 0.08.
the_second_type_that_places_by_a_byte.what_is_still_not_asked: The two 3D types that do not place by a byte. 01 44 is printed with a pre delay and a chorus rate and 01 57 with three delay taps, so there is no placement to hold this byte against on either, and this widens the claim to the two types that place rather than to the four the byte is printed against.
